keyVerseText: Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch, which was the son of Jared, which was the son of Maleleel, which was the son of Cainan,
rootMeaning: The name Μαθουσάλα (Mathousála) originates from the Hebrew מְתוּשֶׁלַח (Methushelach), which can be understood as 'man of the dart.' This etymology suggests a figure associated with strength or a weapon, possibly symbolizing a powerful or enduring individual. The literal sense enriches the common English rendering 'Methuselah' by highlighting an aspect of vigor or active agency embedded in the name, beyond simply being a personal identifier.
usageInScripture: The word Μαθουσάλα appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Luke 3:37, where it is used as a proper noun to identify a key antediluvian patriarch. The top translation, 'Which was the son of Mathusala,' reflects its consistent use as a genealogical marker, emphasizing lineage and heritage. This singular occurrence underscores the name's role in tracing the ancestry of Christ, linking the New Testament to the ancient patriarchal history.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Μαθουσάλα as 'man of the dart' invites reflection on the enduring legacy of faith through generations, as Methuselah stands as a pivotal figure bridging early human history and divine promise. His presence in the genealogy of Christ highlights God's faithfulness in preserving a righteous line despite a fallen world. The name's connotation of strength or weaponry may also metaphorically point to the spiritual resilience required to walk with God amid judgment. Recognizing Methuselah's place in Scripture encourages believers to trust in God's sovereign plan unfolding through history, culminating in the redemptive work of Jesus Christ.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 3:37 traces the lineage of Jesus, stating 'Which was the son of Mathusala, which was the son of Enoch...' Here, Μαθουσάλα serves as a vital link connecting Christ to the antediluvian patriarchs. The inclusion of Methuselah in this genealogy emphasizes the continuity of God's covenantal promises from the earliest days of humanity. The name's meaning enriches the verse by suggesting that Christ's human ancestry is marked by strength and endurance, qualities that reflect the faithfulness of God's people across generations.
